subject: Emotions
title: The Dopamine Hit
description: A fast breakdown of The Dopamine Hit for builders.

hook.text: Rats will press a lever 7,000 times per hour to stimulate their dopamine system—ignoring food, water, and sleep.

buildup.text: Dopamine was once called the 'pleasure chemical.' But neuroscientists now know it's really about wanting, not liking.

discovery.text: Dopamine spikes before the reward, not during it. It's the anticipation of joy, not joy itself.

twist.text: This is why the pursuit feels better than the prize. Shopping beats owning. Chasing beats catching.

climax.text: Social media exploits this: infinite scroll provides endless anticipation with minimal reward. Dopamine without joy.
